name: Maxim and Matrix
description: Maxim loves to fill in a matrix in a special manner. Here is a pseudocode of filling in a matrix of size ( m + 1) × ( m + 1) : Maxim asks you to count, how many numbers m (1 ≤ m ≤ n ) are there, such that the sum of values in the cells in the row number m + 1 of the resulting matrix equals t . Expression ( x xor y ) means applying the operation of bitwise excluding "OR" to numbers x and y . The given operation exists in all modern programming languages. For example, in languages C++ and Java it is represented by character " ^ ", in Pascal — by " xor ".
input_specification: A single line contains two integers n and t (1 ≤ n , t ≤ 10 12 , t ≤ n + 1) . Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in C++ . It is preferred to use the cin , cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output_specification: In a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
